source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Somerset in New Jersey is the second-largest published data center campus in the state, with 23 MW of IT capacity. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this translates to roughly 575 racks, or at 6 GPUs per rack, approximately 3,450 accelerators. Only 5 facilities in New Jersey publish power specifications to the operator level, and Somerset represents about 21 percent of the state's 111.3 MW of disclosed IT capacity.

The campus occupies 185,000 square feet of technical space. No certifications are listed on the operator's published specification page. The site sits in the densest mapped data center region in New Jersey, where 48 facilities have been identified across the state, though most do not disclose capacity figures.

Somerset's rank reflects real capacity but not the full picture of the state's infrastructure. The 43 other mapped facilities in New Jersey likely host additional power and compute, but without published specifications, their contribution to the state's AI-relevant footprint remains unknown. Whether this campus can scale further depends on power availability from the regional grid, which this site has not yet mapped for New Jersey.
